notes.text: I create — I am about wholly to change the state not only of my people, but to bring a new face upon the world, which shall abide until a new heavens and earth appear, in which shall dwell nothing but righteousness. Not be remembered - That state of things shall be so glorious, that the former state of my people shall not be remembered.
You — The church, as well under the gospel, as under the law.

An infant — Those that were now children, shall die at a great age. But - Yet none of these things shall be of any advantage to wicked men, but if any of them shall live to be an hundred years old, yet they shall die accursed.
With them — Is blessed with them.

Before they call — God promised, chap. lviii, 9, to answer them, when they called: here he promises to answer the words, as soon as they should be formed in their hearts before they could get them out of their lips. While - Yea, while they were speaking.

The wolf, &c. — God here promises to take off the fierceness of the spirits of his peoples enemies, so that they shall live quietly and peaceably together. And dust - God promises a time of tranquility to his church under the metaphor of serpents eating the dust, their proper meat, Gen. iii, 14, instead of flying upon men: it signifies such a time, when wicked men shall no more eat up the people of God. God is served with the spirit, and not by ceremonies, ver. 1- 5. The wonderful birth and benefits of the gospel-church, ver. 6- 14. Severe judgments against the wicked, ver. 15-17. The Gentiles shall be an holy church, ver. 18-23. The eternal punishment of the wicked, ver. 24.

glossa.text: *For behold.* Out of angels, namely, and out of men, one Church; and they shall exult and rejoice, that I who created may exult and rejoice in them. *A rejoicing.* Of the whole earth, that she who of old was the joy of the Only-begotten may be, made new, a gladness to all nations. *A joy.* Which we can understand either after the resurrection, or after baptism in the first resurrection. This refers to the general resurrection in which all shall rise again in perfect age. And this is it: *There shall not be,* etc.

*A child of a hundred years,* etc. He, namely, who although he lived long, yet lived childishly, serving the vices: and Gregory expounds this thus. *A child of a hundred years. And a sinner of a hundred years.* The child's life is indeed drawn out long, that he may be corrected from childish deeds: but if he is not restrained from the perpetration of sin even by length of time, this very length of life, which he received through the mercy of God, grows for him unto a heap of malediction.
*Houses.* ((HIER.)) The virtues, for which they shall rest in the heavenly places, etc., *as far as* For many saints build houses, but do not dwell in them.
*For according to.* ((ID.)) As Christ etc., *as far as It is a tree of life to them that have laid hold on her,* namely on wisdom, which is Christ.

*The seed of the blessed.* The apostles, and other teachers in preaching, or in other works, as the Jews, because they shall receive an eternal reward, *for they shall come with joyfulness carrying their sheaves ((Psal. CXXV))*.

*Grandchildren.* Whom their sons have begotten in the faith, as Mark the disciple of Peter, and Luke the son of Paul.
*Before they call.* In trouble, in grief of mind, but in joy and gladness: whence, *For what is our joy or crown of glory, are not you ((II Thes. II))*? etc.

*The wolf.* The wolf is Saul, that is, the persecutor, of whom, *Benjamin a ravenous wolf ((Gen. XLIX))*. *The lamb.* Those, namely, who in white garments follow the lamb whithersoever he goes: of whom it is said to Peter, *Feed my lambs ((Joan. XXI))*. *And the lion and the ox shall eat.* A man, namely, eloquent and most powerful in the world, the eloquence of philosophy being despised, shall eat straw, that is, the usefulness and the surface of the history, with the oxen, that is, with the preachers of the Church. These things the lions eat until by many labours one comes to the depth of the mystery, as Augustine and Cyprian and the rest. *Neither shall they kill.* Their fierceness laid aside, either in the present or in the time to come, and this is it: *In all the mountain,* etc. This the Jews take carnally, saying that in the time of their own Christ there shall be for them so great peace and security that wolves and lambs, lions and oxen, serpents and men shall dwell together, and shall eat, nor shall they harm those who dwell in the temple and on the holy mountain. From which it is gathered that all the rest shall be killed. But that this is false is shown by these words: *Thus saith the Lord: Heaven is my seat, and the earth my footstool,* etc.; yet this too the Jews understand carnally.

notes.text: In that day — When this great work of the reduction of Israel, and conversion of the Gentiles is fulfilled.
God — My salvation hath not been brought to pass by man, but by the almighty power of God.

With joy — Your thirsty souls shall be filled with Divine graces and comforts, which you may draw from God, in the use of gospel-ordinances. God's armies, ver. 1-5. The destruction of Babylon by the Persians and Medes, their great distress, anguish, and utter desolation, ver. 6-22.

glossa.text: *I will give thanks to thee.* ((HIER.)) As, the Red Sea being passed, they said: Let us sing to the Lord, etc. So, the kingdom of the world being destroyed, the Church says: *I will give thanks to thee.*
*Out of the fountains of the Saviour.* ((ID.)) Whence: *Bless ye the Lord from the fountains of Israel,* etc., *as far as* that the prophecy may agree with the Gospel.

notes.text: That walketh disorderly — Particularly by not working. Not according to the tradition he received of us - The admonition we gave, both by word of mouth, and in our former epistle.
Neither let him eat — Do not maintain him in idleness.
Doing nothing, but being busybodies — To which idleness naturally disposes.
Work quietly — Letting the concerns of other people alone.

glossa.text: *We charge.* He begins concerning the curious and the idle, admonishing the good to correct them.

*You know how you ought to imitate us.* And since they do not these things, you ought to shun them. Or, they walk not according to the tradition. For you know how I bore myself, which you do not see in them; as if he should say: There is no need that I should expound to you that tradition, because you know it, namely that we were not restless, as those are who mind other men's business, wandering hither and thither.

*But that we ourselves.* It is to be noted that the Apostle taught not by words only, but exhorted also by deeds. For it belongs to a fit master to fulfil in works the things which he teaches in words.

*For if any man will not work.* Certain men say that the Apostle enjoined this concerning spiritual works; otherwise, if he said this of bodily work, in which either husbandmen or craftsmen labour, he would seem to hold an opinion against the Lord, who says in the Gospel: *Be not solicitous, what you shall eat* ((Matth. VI)), etc. But to no purpose do they strive to draw a mist over both themselves and others, so that they not only wish *velint* to do what charity profitably admonishes, but not even to understand it, since the Apostle in many other places of the epistles most plainly teaches what he here means. For he wills that the servants of God work bodily whereby they may live, that they be not compelled by want to beg for necessaries. Nor is this against that which was said before: *Be not solicitous what you shall eat,* etc. For this was not said to this end, that they should not procure as much as is enough for necessity, from whence they honourably could, but not in order that *sed non ut* they may look upon these things, nor do for the sake of these things whatever they are bidden to do by the proclamation of the Gospel.
*Curiously meddling.* The Lord's discipline abhors this deed, for their god is the belly, who with foul care provide necessaries for themselves.

*Faint not.* Because although they work, yet they may want some things. And therefore he admonishes, lest those who had wherewith to supply necessaries to the servants of God should on this occasion grow slothful. For he does not come under reproof who is kindly in bestowing, but he who, when he could bear labour, wishes to lead his life in idleness.

notes.text: Goodly stones — Such as no engines now in use could have brought, or even set upon each other. Some of them (as an eye witness who lately measured them writes) were forty - five cubits long, five high, and six broad; yet brought thither from another country. And gifts - Which persons delivered from imminent dangers had, in accomplishment of their vows, hung on the walls and pillars. The marble of the temple was so white, that it appeared like a mountain of snow at a distance. And the gilding of many parts made it, especially when the sun shone, a most splendid and beautiful spectacle. Matt. xxiv, 1; Mark xiii, 1.
I am the Christ; and the time is near — When I will deliver you from all your enemies. They are the words of the seducers.
Commotions — Intestine broils; civil wars.
Fearful sights and signs from heaven — Of which Josephus gives a circumstantial account.
Mark xiii, 9.
It shall turn to you for a testimony — Of your having delivered your own souls, and of their being without excuse.
Matt. x, 21.
Matt. xxiv, 13; Mark xiii, 13.
Not a hair of your head — A proverbial expression, shall perish - Without the special providence of God. And then, not before the time, nor without a full reward.

In your patience possess ye your souls — Be calm and serene, masters of yourselves, and superior to all irrational and disquieting passions. By keeping the government of your spirits, you will both avoid much misery, and guard the better against all dangers.

glossa.text: *And some.* After the widow's offering, in which the Church of the Gentiles is signified, the destruction of the temple is subjoined, so that, with the veil of the concealing letter, the hidden sacraments of the Church may begin to be disclosed. For God took care to overthrow the city and the temple and all figurative things, lest anyone after the coming of Christ should run back to them.

*They asked him.* Because to those praising the buildings of the temple he had foretold that all was to be destroyed, the disciples (as Mark says), Peter, James, and John and Andrew, ask apart the time and the signs of the foretold destruction.

*For many.* When the destruction of Jerusalem was at hand, there were many leaders who said that they were Christs and that the time of liberty was drawing near. In the times of the apostles also many heresiarchs came forth, who among their other falsehoods preached that the day of the Lord was at hand, whom the Apostle also refuted.

*Wars and seditions.* These abounded in Judaea from the passion of the Lord; and lest the apostles, terrified by them, should forsake Jerusalem and Judaea, they are warned *that the end is not immediately,* but after the forty-second year.

*Then he said.* Of these, some are from heaven, some from the earth, some from the elements, some from men. Mystically. Kingdom against kingdom, and the pestilence of those whose speech creeps like a canker, and the famine of hearing the word of God, the shaking of the earth, the separation from the true faith, ought to be understood of heretics, who, fighting against one another, make the victory of the Church. *And great signs.* These also are found fulfilled at that time in Josephus, who relates that a star like a sword hung over Jerusalem for a year, and that chariots and armed horsemen fought in the air for forty days, and that a heifer brought forth a lamb among the hands of those sacrificing.

*And it shall happen,* etc. Of those who either persecute, or are not changed by their living. For the death of the just is to the good a help, to the wicked a testimony of damnation, so that the perverse may perish without excuse from that whence the elect take an example that they may live.

*By parents,* etc. It is a greater torment when a man suffers from those upon whom he counted, because along with the loss of the body the evils of lost charity torment him. And because the things foretold of the affliction of death are hard, a consolation concerning the joy of the resurrection is subjoined.

*And a hair.* As if he said: Why do you fear that that should perish which hurts when cut, seeing that not even there can that perish in you which does not hurt when cut? For the flesh when cut hurts, the hair does not hurt.

*In your patience.* Patience is the root and the guardian of all the virtues. In it therefore we possess our souls, which possess the body, when we govern those souls by reason unto suffering. But true patience is to endure with equanimity the evils of another, and to be moved by no grief against him who inflicts the evils.

notes.text: Cometh — Tho' it be at a distance from you, yet it is coming and will overtake you and overwhelm you too. As an oven - The refiner's fire, chap. iii, 2, is now represented as a fire, burning more dreadfully, as it did indeed when Jerusalem and the temple were on fire, when the fire raged everywhere, but most fiercely where the arched roofs made it double itself, and infold flames with flames. And this may well be an emblem of the day of judgment.

The sun of righteousness — Christ, who is fitly compared to the sun, being the fountain of light, and vital heat to his church. And of mercy and benignity; for the Hebrew word imports both. With healing - His beams shall bring health and strength, with delight and joy, safety and security. Go forth - Go out of Jerusalem, before the fatal siege. Grow up - In strength, vigour and spiritual stature. Of the stall - Where they are safe guarded and well ordered.

Salvation — The redemption of the world by the Messiah: which was hitherto reserved was a secret among the Jews, yea was not throughly known by the most of the Jews themselves. Righteousness - His faithfulness in accomplishing this great promise. Israel is required to praise God, for their hasty constitution both in church and state, ver. 1-5. Some instances of the happy administration of it, ver. 6-9.

glossa.text:
*Sing ye to the Lord.* ((CASS.)) First he speaks of the showing forth of the saving right hand.

*He hath saved.* ((AUG.)) It is a greater thing that he raised up the whole world from eternal death, than that he raised the dead. *To himself.* Many are saved bodily, but to themselves, not to him: they who, having received bodily health, grow wanton, but they who by faith are healed within, are healed to him, or save themselves.

*Salvation . . . justice.* ((AUG.)) He who saves and justifies. *He hath revealed.* Things to come were foretold under a veil by the prophets: but the veil has been taken away, since *truth is sprung out of the earth.*

*Of mercy and of truth.* ((AUG.)) *Mercy* is that whereby he promised, *truth* follows upon this, because he rendered it. But to whom? *To Israel,* that is, to him who now by faith sees the truth, afterwards by sight.
*All.* ((ID.)) Because Christ was not given to certain men only.
*Rejoice ye.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he says that in all ways he is to be praised and declared, because the judge is come.

*With ductile trumpets and with the voice of a trumpet of horn.* ((AUG.)) Of brass, which are drawn out by beating, etc., *as far as* as the horn cleaves to the flesh, and surpasses it. ((HIERON.)) With ductile trumpets, of silver, after the manner of the Jews. Mystically, drawn out under the hammer of the whole earth, that is, the devil. ((AUG.)) Tribulation is the beating; advancement, the drawing out: such a trumpet was Job, whence he sounded as a trumpet, saying: *The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away.*

*Let it be moved.* ((ID.)) That is, let the sea of the law be made sweet, the wood of the cross being set therein. *And the fulness thereof.* All the sacraments of the law, etc., *as far as* but *the rivers,* etc. *The earth.* ((CASS.)) That is, every sinner.

*The world of the earth.* All earthly men. *In justice.* ((AUG.)) Because they did not merit mercy. *The peoples.* ((CASS.)) The faithful out of the Jews and the Gentiles, who shall receive things equal to their merits.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Sing to the Lord, for he has done marvelous things.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
Do not be terrified; by your endurance you will gain your souls.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
He is coming to judge the earth with righteousness.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The day is coming, the prophet says, burning like an oven — but not for everyone the same way.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
For those who revere God's name, the dawn breaks with warmth, with healing in its wings.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
So when the world shakes and rumors fly, do not be terrified; not a hair of your head is lost.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
By your endurance you will gain your souls; sing now to the God who is coming to set things right.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The day comes burning; the dawn breaks with healing.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
Do not be terrified; not a hair is lost.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing.
By your endurance you will gain your souls.
The sun of righteousness will rise with healing. Amen.
